chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Jack Lesberg's invitation to Dick Gibson's party
summary: Jack Lesberg mentioned a rich man's yearly party in Colorado and a year later arranged for Gus to be paid $400 to attend.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So, Gus, we're talking now about -- all right, Gus, so now what we wanted to talk about was that World's Greatest -- so Lesberg came in.

Oh, yeah, that's right. And Jack came in the club there. I was playing there, with Zoot and Al Cohen. And so I went over and spoke to him during intermission, like I came over and I said, 'Hey, Jack, where have you been? I haven't seen you in a long time,' like that.

So he said, 'Well, I've been out in Colorado, been playing for a party out there. For a rich guy that has a party every year.' So I said, 'Well, how come you didn't take me with you, just kidding.' So he said, 'Well, he had about four or five drummers. And so he didn't need another drummer.' I said, 'Well, talk him into getting me out there,' just like that.
And he said, 'Well, I will. Cliff Leeman, he's been kind of sick. And maybe something might happen to get you out there.' So I said, 'Well, that's great.'
And then, first one thing and then the other, and I didn't see him anymore after that.

So the next year, I did get a call. And I answered the phone and I said, 'Hello?' And he said, 'Hey, Gus, this is Jack.' I said, 'Yeah, Jack, what's happening?' He said, 'Well, I got you that job out there, if you want it, playing the party.' I said, 'You've got to be kidding.' And he said, 'No, really.' He said, 'If you want to play it, you can play it.

I said, 'Well, sure, I'd like to play it, just like that. And so he said, 'Well, I'll let you talk to Dick Gibson. He'll call you later on. So I just called to let you know. And you might play and you might not,' he said. 'Because Cliff Leeman is ill and if he can't make it, then you'll have to play. But if he can make it, you won't play. But he will pay you anyway.
He wanted you to come out anyway.
Yes, he said, 'And the room is free and food is free. And you get $400 for coming out.'
I said, 'Well, that's all right with me. I can't lose on nothing like that.'
And so I went out. I came out here. And I met him.
